narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have similarly limited experience, while the rest tend to have six or more years. This lack of broader career history appears to signal higher turnover risk to the system.

The second most influential factor was that you have received other job offers while at your current company. This strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving, as having external opportunities often indicates that someone is considering or actively exploring options elsewhere.

Third, working in the “other” sector also contributed to the prediction of leaving. This sector shows a noticeably higher likelihood of departure compared with fields like medicine or education, where more employees are expected to remain.

Although several positive elements exist in your profile, such as having medical insurance, no overtime demands, and general job satisfaction, these were not strong enough to outweigh the top three influences.

The organization should consider discussing your career development goals with you and exploring ways to build your experience internally. You may want to reflect on whether the external opportunities you’ve received better align with your long-term plans. Addressing these areas could improve your prospects for future advancement.
